PASS applies solely to restricted A–E for the entire declared rotational class R. The current author proof and complete notes n1–n3 establish the requested conclusions. Original unrestricted S02 remains incomplete. Neither historical INCONCLUSIVE report is amended, and the historical invalid bindings 13–16 are not inherited. Metadata, symbolic-check verdicts and previous reviews were not used as mathematical premises.

The external foundations below have fresh, consistent indices and complete matching quotations from the expressly permitted foundations. Task-specific Hopf conventions, canonical representatives, compatible non-pluripolar measures and restricted-depth estimates are applied directly as problem assumptions. In particular, the applicable grants are: “Define its extended non-pluripolar measure mu_u=MA_ext_omega(u) by the increasing compatible measures 1_{u>-k}(omega+dd^c max(u,-k))^3; the product for bounded quasi-psh functions is the local Bedford--Taylor expansion against the smooth background. The pole set has measure zero, and total mass is allowed to be infinite.” And: “The known restricted-depth bound is mu_u({u>=-T})<=C(1+T), and mu_u(A intersect {u>=-T})<=(1+T)^3 Cap_omega(A).” These grants are used for their stated measures and original capacity.

The normalization and smooth estimate check out. Simultaneously dividing the Xia–Zhang operator and background by 2π leaves scalar potentials unchanged. Direct differentiation verifies the local matrix for every finite x; endpoint assumptions are required for the constructed family’s extension, not for that local calculation. The determinant, normalized radial Fubini–Study density and probability fiber area give MAω(V)=12AΔ dx dΩ dA, also for semipositive matrices without division by the vertical coefficient. Periodic integration gives ∫EΔ=m″+μ(1−μ)−e″/2. Fiber means and vertical Dirichlet integrals are smooth invariant functions on the base. Their x derivatives vanish at both ends, including the positive end where the pointwise potential can retain fiber dependence. Hence ∫Δ=1. Positivity gives Vxx≥−1; semiconvexity with displacement Vx and V≤0 proves |Vx|²≤−2V. Thus ∫MAω(V)/(1+√(−2V))≤12, yielding exactly 12Q(W) and 12Q_T(W). The relevant source normalization and local hypotheses were checked against [Xia–Zhang](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.21053v1).

The passage to every bounded member of R is valid. Both capacity comparisons use fixed inner and outer coordinate balls. The reverse gluing parameters can be chosen with aR²<1 and ε<a(R²−r²), producing an actual global competitor in [−1,0]. Positive product comparisons follow by regularizing locally corrected psh functions, allowing a vanishing quadratic positivity error, and passing bounded mixed products to the limit. The transitive compact group preserves ω and acts holomorphically. Lifting to the group and differentiating the convolution kernel proves smoothing; centrality preserves U(2) invariance. Quasi-continuity, capacity invariance and the displayed Markov estimate prove convergence in the original capacity.

For bounded products, the telescoping integration-by-parts formula is applied only to corrected local psh functions and compactly supported smooth test forms. Mixed trace measures, including quadratic factors, are dominated by local capacity by expanding a normalized bounded psh sum. Splitting at |p_j−p|≤δ proves convergence in every degree. Expanding against γ=dd^cρ−ω then handles the Hermitian product; derivatives of γ remain inside the smooth test coefficients. No closedness of γ or ω is assumed. Quasi-continuity, continuous extension and uniform capacity domination justify the depth weights. These applications satisfy the local hypotheses of [Bedford–Taylor](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf). Their operator is 4π times the present one, so the local capacity constants are rescaled accordingly.

Compatible strict truncations and monotone convergence extend the estimates to every unbounded genuine member of R. Splitting at depth T gives the exact Borel bound W(0)(1+T)³Capω(A)+12Q_T(W). Fixed truncations preserve capacity convergence. For K>1, replacing u by max(u,−K) changes its weighted measure by total variation at most 24Q_{K−1}(W). Both measures on the entire floor set {u≤−K} are bounded by the tail estimate, including possible truncation mass on {u=−K}. Consequently Q_T→0 proves uniform absolute continuity and weighted weak continuity.

The faster-scale family is globally admissible. The completed-square identity follows directly from the heat equation and the chain rule. Its source estimate applies on the linear region with the required t, μ, η and κ, and on the initial region with κχ²; χ=0 is checked separately. At ε=exp(−cη⁻³), the defect integral is O(ℓ)+o(1), rather than o(1). A fixed sufficiently small c therefore supplies every correction margin. The terminal cutoff error is smaller than the background radial positivity because ℓ<1/(10e). The correction removes the Schur-complement defect and keeps the angular coefficient positive. Its eventual constancy gives global smooth extension. The negative-end fiber mean gives 0≤sup Vη≤Cη, so the normalization is canonical and the global depth is bounded by Bη⁻².

On the actual core annuli, tk_t is bounded above and below, h→∞, ζ→0, μ→1 and ησ²t→0 uniformly. The completed square tends to one, while the remaining negative terms are controlled. Hence Q≥1/4, A≥cησ and the vertical coefficient is at least cη/t. The annular fiber area is exactly 3t/2. Integrating the actual density gives mass at least Dη⁻¹ at depths between Aη⁻² and Bη⁻². This verifies both the author construction and n2’s equivalent parameterization. Matching every sufficiently large t=Bη⁻² proves necessity for arbitrary decreasing weights, including oscillating square-root profiles.

The single infinite-measure argument establishes the stronger individual obstruction. Controlled corrections have uniform derivative bounds on fixed product neighborhoods away from w=0 and a global slope bound. C* is fixed before choosing scales. All separation, depth, future-series and derivative constraints can be met along arbitrarily large values of √t W(t). The supplied submean propagation through a connected finite chart cover gives a uniform L¹ bound without BMP. The decreasing series consequently has a genuine canonical quasi-psh limit with current margin 3ω/4. Its canonical limiting assertions match the permitted [Demailly foundations](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf). On each selected core neighborhood the series converges smoothly, and the determinant inequality gives the actual local measure lower bound a_j³MAω(u_j). Supremum normalization decreases depths. The disjoint cores each contribute at least one, proving infinite weighted mass for one actual invariant potential.

The necessity arguments for C and D also use actual measures. The cores approach the analytic divisor H={z0=0}. Local polar-capacity zero and decreasing compact-capacity continuity, transferred through the proved comparisons, imply their original capacities tend to zero. The controlled correction masses converge to m>0. Near H, the limiting function is m log|n|²−m log(1+|ζ|²)+constant. This proves its genuine logarithmic extension, canonical value −∞ on H and positive divisor contribution; the smooth current remains semipositive by the established margins and continuity across H. Its supremum is zero. Away from H, heat exceptional sets lie in exponentially shrinking tubes about the locally analytic section w=0. Their capacities vanish, and the corrections converge uniformly on compact affine regions. Removing a small-capacity neighborhood of H proves actual original-capacity convergence uη→g.

In the bounded nonvanishing square-root regime, the full weighted measures are uniformly finite. A weak cluster exists, and Portmanteau on each closed neighborhood of H, followed by decreasing continuity, forces positive cluster mass on H. The actual νW,g gives H zero mass. This is the requested finite-measure discontinuity example. In the unbounded square-root regime, the single infinite measure instead obstructs a finite-measure map on all of R.

The additional floor calculations in n2 are correct. For large k, write g(x_k)=−k and μ_k=μ(x_k). Away from H the radial density is 6d(A²), giving μ_g(X)=6(1−m)². Smooth convex regularizations of the bounded truncation converge uniformly and preserve positivity. Bounded product convergence gives boundary mass 6[μ_k²−(μ_k−m)²], floor-interior mass 6(1−μ_k²), and entire floor-level mass 6[1−(μ_k−m)²]. The strict restriction has mass 6(μ_k−m)², whereas μ_g({g=−k})=0. Thus no boundary-level product mass is discarded.

Accordingly, A holds exactly when √t W(t) is bounded at infinity; B–D hold exactly when √t W(t)→0. The power/logarithmic asymptotic t^(1/2−p)(log t)^−a proves E with precisely the stated boundaries. The P07 excerpt is valid at its used compactness scope. The closed-elliptic diagnostic has consistent normalization and energy calculations and supplies no global Hopf counterexample. The reproduced general damping proof follows from the granted depth bounds and the checked bounded-product passage. Xia–Zhang’s heat construction and the known damping background receive the stated credit. Unrestricted sharp sufficiency remains unresolved.

Two historical wording corrections are harmless: sup[−(Wη)x]₋ must read sup[(Wη)x]₋; at T=0 the tail bound follows from the total estimate, while at T>0 the cutoff argument uses 0<δ<T. Neither requires a substantive repair of the current restricted argument. No essential mathematical check remains unsettled.

passages.statement: On the scalar Hopf threefold, with dd^c_src=i∂bar∂ and omega_src=i∂bar∂s+i∂s∧bar∂s, s=log|z|², set xi=z'/z0, w=log z0, x=log|xi|² and mu=e^x/(1+e^x). For smooth real V(x,w), its local Hermitian matrix in the alpha_src-unit tangential, alpha_src-unit radial and ∂/∂w frame is [[(mu+V_x)/mu,0,0],[0,(mu+V_xx)/(mu(1-mu)),(mu+V_xbarw)/sqrt(mu(1-mu))],[0,(mu+V_wx)/sqrt(mu(1-mu)),1+V_wbarw]]. If V is independent of x for sufficiently negative x and constant in x,w for sufficiently positive x, it extends smoothly globally; positivity at xi=0 is equivalent to 1+V_wbarw>0. Xia–Zhang, Lemma 2.2.
passages.quote: On the scalar Hopf threefold, with dd^c_src=i partial barpartial and omega_src=i partial barpartial s+i partial s wedge barpartial s, s=log|z|^2, put xi=z'/z0, w=log z0, x=log|xi|^2 and mu=e^x/(1+e^x). For smooth real V(x,w), its local Hermitian matrix in the alpha_src-unit tangential, alpha_src-unit radial and partial/partial w frame is [[(mu+V_x)/mu,0,0],[0,(mu+V_xx)/(mu(1-mu)),(mu+V_xbarw)/sqrt(mu(1-mu))],[0,(mu+V_wx)/sqrt(mu(1-mu)),1+V_wbarw]]. If V is independent of x for sufficiently negative x and constant in x,w for sufficiently positive x, it extends smoothly globally; positivity at xi=0 is equivalent to 1+V_wbarw>0.

passages.statement: For an open Omega⊂C^n and locally bounded genuine psh functions p1,...,pk, 1≤k≤n, their Bedford–Taylor mixed product is a positive closed current, local and symmetric multilinear in its arguments, and weakly continuous under simultaneous decreasing locally bounded psh limits whose limits are locally bounded. Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.
passages.quote: For Omega contained in C^n and locally bounded genuine psh p1,...,pk, k<=n, their Bedford--Taylor mixed product is a positive closed current, local and symmetric multilinear in its arguments, and weakly continuous under simultaneous decreasing locally bounded psh limits.

passages.statement: For locally bounded psh p,q on an open Omega⊂C^n, compactly supported smooth (n-k,n-k)-forms phi, and 1≤k≤n, ∫phi[(dd^c p)^k-(dd^c q)^k]=Σ_(l=0)^(k-1)∫(p-q)dd^c phi∧(dd^c p)^l∧(dd^c q)^(k-1-l). Bedford–Taylor, Corollary 2.8 and its mixed-degree integration-by-parts consequence.
passages.quote: For locally bounded psh p,q on Omega contained in C^n and compactly supported smooth (n-k,n-k)-forms phi,1<=k<=n, int phi[(dd^c p)^k-(dd^c q)^k]=sum_(l=0)^(k-1) int(p-q)dd^c phi wedge(dd^c p)^l wedge(dd^c q)^(k-1-l).

passages.statement: For K compactly contained in an open Omega⊂C^n, bounded psh p1,...,pk with 1≤k≤n, and the Euclidean Kähler form beta, ∫_K dd^c p1∧...∧dd^c pk∧beta^(n-k)≤C_(K,Omega,k)Π_i||pi||_L∞(Omega). Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.10.
passages.quote: For K compactly contained in Omega contained in C^n, bounded psh p1,...,pk,k<=n, and the Euclidean Kahler form beta, int_K dd^c p1 wedge...wedge dd^c pk wedge beta^(n-k)<=C_(K,Omega,k) product_i ||pi||_L^infinity(Omega).

passages.statement: On a bounded domain Omega⊂C^n, every genuine psh function is quasi-continuous for relative Bedford–Taylor capacity: for each epsilon>0 there is an open O⊂Omega with C(O,Omega)<epsilon such that the function restricted to Omega\O is continuous. Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 3.5.
passages.quote: On a bounded domain Omega contained in C^n, every genuine psh function is quasi-continuous for relative Bedford--Taylor capacity: for each epsilon>0 there is an open O contained in Omega with C(O,Omega)<epsilon such that its restriction to Omega minus O is continuous.

passages.statement: On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain Omega⊂C^n, every locally pluripolar set has zero outer Bedford–Taylor capacity. Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 6.9.
passages.quote: On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain Omega contained in C^n, every locally pluripolar set has zero outer Bedford--Taylor capacity.

passages.statement: On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain Omega⊂C^n, if compact subsets K_j decrease to K, then C(K_j,Omega) decreases to C(K,Omega); also C*(K,Omega)=C(K,Omega). Bedford–Taylor, Proposition 6.4.
passages.quote: On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex Omega contained in C^n, if compact subsets K_j decrease to K, then C(K_j,Omega) decreases to C(K,Omega); also C*(K,Omega)=C(K,Omega).

passages.statement: On an open Omega⊂C^n, a decreasing sequence of genuine psh functions has a genuine locally integrable psh pointwise limit whenever the limit is not identically -∞ on any component. A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. The cone Psh(Omega)∩L1_loc(Omega) is closed in L1_loc(Omega), and its L1_loc-bounded subsets are relatively compact. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, I.4.17, I.5.4 and I.5.8–5.9.
passages.quote: On an open Omega contained in C^n, a decreasing sequence of genuine psh functions has a genuine locally integrable psh pointwise limit whenever the limit is not identically minus infinity on any component. A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. The cone Psh(Omega) intersect L1_loc(Omega) is closed in L1_loc, and its L1_loc-bounded subsets are relatively compact.
